notes: Page numbers are PDF page numbers (the pypdf text and the PDF itself, 43 pages); the booklet's printed page number is 6 lower (PDF p41 = printed Page 35). The docling text skips blank pages, so its page markers run 2 to 3 lower than the PDF from page 13 on; reading A's cites used those and were corrected here.

Brackets: the booklet prints one rate schedule (PDF p41) for every filing status; it is recorded under single and married_joint only. A detailed tax table is only on the Department's website, not in the booklet.

Filing statuses: 1 = Single, 2 = Joint, 3 = Married filing separately; a federal head of household files as Filing Status 1 and fills in the Head of Household oval (PDF p15). So head_of_household amounts below are the Filing Status 1 amounts. The booklet does not mention a qualifying surviving spouse.

Standard deduction: 8,750 (Filing Status 1 and 3) and 17,500 (Filing Status 2) for Taxable Years 2025 and 2026. The booklet says the increase is scheduled to sunset after Taxable Year 2026 and revert to the amounts that applied before Taxable Year 2019: 3,000 for single filers and 6,000 for married couples filing jointly (PDF p7 What's New; PDF p17 Line 11). Only the 2025 amounts are recorded as figures; the scheduled change is kept here in notes (scheduled changes are a separate pending feature, tax-reference-data issue #2).

A filer who itemized on the federal return must itemize on Virginia Schedule A (Line 10, PDF p17); itemized amounts are not recorded. A person claimed as a dependent on another's return is limited to the smaller of earned income or the standard deduction (PDF p19).

Exemptions: 930 times the sum of the You, Spouse and Dependents boxes; 800 times the sum of the 65-or-older and Blind boxes (PDF p15; Form 760 page 1 Exemption Sections A and B). The 65-or-older and blind exemptions cannot be claimed with the Credit for Low-Income Individuals (Line 23).

Age Deduction (Form 760 Line 4): recorded as two entries by birth date (on or before 1939-01-01: 12,000 each, no income test; 1939-01-02 to 1961-01-01: income based). No minimum age is printed apart from the birth dates, so min_age is left out. Born after 1961-01-01: the booklet prints no age deduction (PDF p15: 'taxpayers born on or before January 1, 1961, may qualify').

Income-based age deduction: married taxpayers always use the joint AFAGI of both spouses, filing jointly or separately, against 75,000; if both spouses claim, the joint deduction (2 x 12,000 less the excess) is computed first and half allocated to each (PDF p16 worksheet lines 1-15; PDF p17). The schema's income_test cannot say that the reduction is taken once from the combined maximum; that is in cap_rule.

The age deduction and the disability income subtraction are alternatives for each spouse (best_of_group age_or_disability; PDF p15 Line 4, PDF p25 Line 5). The bar on claiming the age deduction together with the Credit for Low-Income Individuals, the Virginia Earned Income Credit or the Refundable Virginia Earned Income Credit is in other_conditions, because credits have no ids in this record.

Social Security: Form 760 Line 5 subtracts Social Security and equivalent Tier 1 Railroad Retirement benefits taxable on the federal return (Form 760 page 1 Line 5; PDF p17 Line 5; also taken out of AFAGI on worksheet line 7, PDF p16). Recorded as exempt.

Pensions, IRAs, 401(k), Roth conversions: the booklet prints no general Virginia subtraction for private or public pensions, IRA or employer-plan distributions, and does not mention Roth conversions; not found in the booklet. The age deduction applies against any income. Treatment of another state's government pension is not found in the booklet, apart from code 31 (retirement income whose contributions another state taxed).
Code 31 (retirement income previously taxed by another state) covers 'other_income' because the booklet names only 'retirement income'; the retirement kinds it may take are in covers_unclear.

Military: the booklet lists three subtractions for servicemembers (combat zone pay code 30, basic pay code 38, Virginia National Guard code 28; PDF p25) and the same income may not be in more than one; recorded as covering wages. Military retirement: code 60 (40,000 per person) and code 44 (Medal of Honor recipients).

Municipal interest: Schedule ADJ Line 1 adds interest on obligations of other states not included in federal AGI, 'which is taxable in Virginia' (PDF p23); code 20 subtracts income from Virginia obligations, including interest on Virginia state bonds or municipal obligations and gains on their sale, to the extent in federal AGI (PDF p25). Code 10 adds interest or dividends exempt from federal tax but taxable in Virginia (PDF p24); Line 4 subtracts income from U.S. obligations (PDF p25).

Capital gains: no rate or deduction share for gains differs from ordinary income in the booklet; capital_gains is empty. The narrow code 52 subtraction (qualified-business investments made 2010-2020) is in reliefs.

Spouse Tax Adjustment (Form 760 Line 17): a reduction of tax of up to 259 on a joint return, figured from each spouse's separate VAGI on the worksheet on PDF p18; the schema has no field for it, and it is not a recapture.
Filing threshold: tax is 0 if VAGI is less than 11,950 (Filing Status 1 or 3) or 23,900 (Filing Status 2) (Form 760 Line 9; PDF p17 Line 9); no field holds this.

Left out of reliefs: Schedule ADJ subtractions unrelated to retirement, wages or investment income (lottery prizes under 600, Holocaust assets, Work Opportunity Tax Credit wages, Commonwealth Savers distributions, land preservation, historic rehabilitation, first-time home buyer accounts, student loan discharge, eminent domain gain, federal partnership income, other); the additions other than municipal and U.S. obligation interest; Schedule ADJ deductions (lines 8a-8c); and credits.

Indexing: the booklet says nothing about inflation adjustment for any figure. The standard deduction is no (2026-11-08): What's New (PDF p7) says legislation set it for Taxable Years 2025 and 2026 and that it reverts after 2026 to the pre-2019 amounts, so it is fixed by law, not adjusted. Every other entry is not_stated. No surtax and no recapture is printed.

Settlement 2026-11-07: muni_interest.treatment: A said other_states_taxed_own_exempt, B said other; PDF p23 Schedule ADJ Line 1 adds interest on obligations of other states as 'taxable in Virginia' and PDF p25 code 20 subtracts interest on Virginia state bonds or municipal obligations, so other_states_taxed_own_exempt.

Settlement 2026-11-07: military_basic_pay.income_test: A recorded a dollar-for-dollar test on military basic pay over 15,000 (measure other), B put it only in cap_rule; PDF p26 code 38 prints 'For every $1.00 of income over $15,000, the maximum subtraction is reduced by $1.00', so A's income_test is kept.

Settlement 2026-11-07: annuity_death_benefit (code 49), combat_zone_pay (code 30), retirement_prev_taxed_other_state (code 31): who.basis: A said return, B said each_person; PDF p26-27 prints no age test, no per-person cap and no each-spouse rule for these codes (unlike codes 38, 39 and 60, which say each spouse may qualify), so return, the schema's value when no person's age or limit is used.

Settlement 2026-11-07: retirement_prev_taxed_other_state.covers_unclear: only B listed ira_distribution, employer_plan_distribution, private_pension, public_pension_other_state; PDF p26 code 31 says only 'retirement income', which leaves the kinds open, so B's list is kept.
Settlement 2026-11-07: lottery_prizes (code 24): only B recorded it; out of scope with the other minor Schedule ADJ subtractions both readers left out; dropped.

Settlement 2026-11-07: standard_deduction and age_deduction_income_based threshold: head_of_household added at the Filing Status 1 amounts (8,750; 50,000) because a federal head of household files Virginia Filing Status 1 (PDF p15); neither reader had it.
Settlement 2026-11-07: indexing standard_deduction: B put the scheduled sunset in 'index' (what a figure is indexed to); moved to notes, since the booklet states no inflation index.
